dn1:1.4.4: “Sir, when we had risen at the crack of dawn and were sitting together in the pavilion, the topic of judgmentalism came up:
dn1:1.4.5: ‘It’s incredible, reverends, it’s amazing how the diverse convictions of sentient beings have been well deciphered by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.
dn1:1.4.6: For this Suppiya criticizes the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha in many ways,
dn1:1.4.7: while his pupil Brahmadatta praises them in many ways.
dn1:1.4.8: And so both tutor and pupil followed behind the Buddha and the Saṅgha of mendicants directly contradicting each other.’
dn1:2.6.2: Those beings who were reborn later are shorter-lived, less beautiful, and less illustrious.
dn1:3.58.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins assert that the self and the cosmos are eternal on four grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.59.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins assert that the self and the cosmos are partially eternal and partially not eternal on four grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.60.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins assert that the cosmos is finite or infinite on four grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.61.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins who are endless flip-floppers, whenever they’re asked a question, resort to verbal flip-flops and endless flip-flops on four grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.62.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins assert that the self and the cosmos arose anomalously on two grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.63.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins who speculate and theorize about the first beginning propose various hypotheses concerning the first beginning on eighteen grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.64.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins who say there is life after death, and assert that the self lives on after death in a percipient form on sixteen grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.65.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins who say there is life after death, and assert that the self lives on after death in a non-percipient form on eight grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.66.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins who say there is life after death, and assert that the self lives on after death in a neither percipient nor non-percipient form on eight grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.67.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins assert the annihilation, eradication, and nonexistence of an existing being on seven grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.68.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins assert ultimate extinguishment for an existing being in this life on five grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.69.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins who speculate and theorize about the final end propose various hypotheses concerning the final end on forty-four grounds, it is not possible that they should experience these things without contact.
dn1:3.71.1: Now, when those ascetics and brahmins assert that the self and the cosmos are eternal on four grounds, and those ascetics and brahmins who are partial eternalists …
dn1:3.71.2: and those ascetics and brahmins who say the cosmos is finite or infinite …
dn1:3.71.3: and those ascetics and brahmins who are endless flip-floppers …
dn1:3.71.4: and those ascetics and brahmins who assert anomalous origination …
dn1:3.71.5: and those ascetics and brahmins who speculate and theorize about the first beginning …
dn1:3.71.6: and those ascetics and brahmins who say there is life after death in a percipient form …
dn1:3.71.7: and those ascetics and brahmins who say there is life after death in a non-percipient form …
dn1:3.71.8: and those ascetics and brahmins who say there is life after death in a neither percipient nor non-percipient form …
dn1:3.71.9: and those ascetics and brahmins who assert annihilation …
dn1:3.71.10: and those ascetics and brahmins who speak of extinguishment in this life …
dn1:3.71.11: and those ascetics and brahmins who speculate and theorize about the final end …
dn1:3.74.7: The Divine Net is finished—the first.
